about: Rules for the combined timeline (public/timelines/ancient-classical.json), generated from the compiled Ancient and
Classical files by `npm run data -- combine` (scripts/lib/combine.ts). Don't edit the generated file: fix the data in
data-src/ancient-near-east.json or data-src/classical.json, or a rule here, and run the command again.
General rules (in the code, not listed here): Ancient's version of a shared row or event wins (name, colour, link,
description, importance) except as listed below; a shared row's lifespan starts as Ancient gives it and ends as
Classical gives it; phases are merged by name (Classical's wins a tie); rows keep the dating system they had in
Ancient; a source key that the two files define differently is split, Classical's copy getting the suffix
'-classical'. Sibling rows keep Ancient's order, with Classical's rows slotted in after their Classical neighbour.
The command stops on any new conflict (a shared row with a different parent, a shared event with a different title)

meta.title: Ancient and Classical World
meta.subtitle: From the first farmers to the rise of Islam: Europe, Africa, the Near East, Asia, Oceania and the Americas, c. 9000 BCE – 650 CE
meta.description: Ancient Civilizations and The Classical World on one chart, from the Neolithic to the fall of the Sasanians and the founding of Tang. Rows from both are merged by region; where the two give the same row different dates, its start follows Ancient Civilizations and its end The Classical World.

rome.why: Ancient's Rome row and Classical's Rome (Republic, then Empire) are the same state: one row, with the Kingdom phase from Ancient.

greece.why: Classical's Greece group holds what Ancient's Aegean group holds (Ancient uses the id greece for the Archaic and Classical Greece row).

persia.why: Classical's 'Iran and Mesopotamia' group becomes Ancient's Iran group; the id persia stays Ancient's Achaemenid Persia row.

south-asia.why: Both are the South Asia group; Ancient's id is indus.

celts.why: La Tène Celts (Gaul) in Classical is Ancient's La Tène (Celts) row, with the same lifespan.

carthage.why: As in Classical: Carthage sits beside Numidia and Mauretania, its neighbours and later rivals.

dmt.why: As in Classical: Dʿmt sits in the Horn of Africa group, before Aksum.

nubia.why: As in Ancient: Nubia stays inside Egypt's group, since Egypt and Kush interacted throughout; Classical's group sits in Africa.

rome-republic-empire.why: As in Classical: Rome is its own group (with the Eastern Roman Empire), between the western Mediterranean and Greece.

near-east.why: With Classical's rows added, Arabia and Egypt share more events: the proximity test needs them closer (scored with scripts/row-order.ts; 184 against 204 for Ancient's order).

aegean.to: Aegean, Greece and the Hellenistic world
aegean.why: The group now runs from the Cycladic culture to the Hellenistic kingdoms.

egypt.why: Ancient's name: Nubia stays inside the group.

nubia.why: Classical's name: the group now runs to Makuria and Alodia.

zhangzhung.why: Classical's name: Yarlung has its own row here.

rome-republic-empire.why: The merged row carries all three phases.

iran.why: The group runs from the Zagros farmers to the Sasanians; Ancient's name, spelled out.

classical.buni: Classical has a Buni culture row; Ancient files it under Indonesia.
classical.kalanay: Classical has a Sa Huỳnh–Kalanay row; Ancient files it under the Philippines.
classical.nyatri-tsenpo: Classical has a Yarlung row; Ancient files the first Yarlung king under Zhangzhung.

eventsWorded.plain-ware: Classical rewrote this event in its Oceania pass (other rows, other wording); Ancient's version is used, which carries the translation-notice disclosure.
